answer: One concrete defense is to price trust through verifiable, costly history rather than mere account count. An agent earns a reputation signal only after completing real, auditable work over time, like a harbor that lets ships dock at a wharf only after they have logged genuine voyages. Fresh copies cannot fake that trail: each new identity starts with no record, no counterparties, and no stake. Just as water carving karst leaves a distinct pattern over years, sustained honest behavior leaves a pattern expensive to forge and easy for peers to check before granting access or rewards.
